claim: Three statements in this bead's own leaves, all true at origin/main, are now false. (1) test_graph_structure.md's Setup paragraph: "DAGChecker fixtures cover four shapes only — `dag_valid` ..., `dag_module_cycle` ..., `dag_req_cycle` and `dag_comp_cycle`; the remaining DAG scenarios have no dedicated fixture, and each carries a note below saying what covers it, if anything." (2) arch_dag_checker.md's "Graphs Checked" paragraph: "The entry's message names which graph it came from — under the default profile: module, requirement or component dependency." (3) test_graph_structure.md's D9: "under the default profile ... the graphs that can actually cycle are exactly the three the scenarios above exercise, the other four passing vacuously."
authoritative_source: This bead's own D9 scenario ("Acyclicity over profile-declared edges") and its two variants, further down the same leaf, describe behavior that the fixtures `dag_profile_edge_cycle`, `dag_profile_edge_cyclic_exempt` and `dag_profile_builtin_exempt` now realize end-to-end in validator/dag_checker_test.go. The project-scoped requirement `depends_on` graph the same bead's scope-aware `builtinDAGEdgeCoverage` routes to the generic path (`validator/dag_checker.go`, `checkExtraProjectDAGEdges`) is a fourth graph that can actually cycle under the default profile, exercised by `dag_project_req_cycle` and `TestREQ3_ProjectRequirementDependencyCycle`.
evidence: This PR adds six checked-in fixture directories under validator/testdata/ — dag_profile_edge_cycle, dag_profile_edge_cyclic_exempt, dag_profile_builtin_exempt, dag_profile_omits_builtin_edges, dag_profile_data_flow_uses_cycle and dag_project_req_cycle — driven by new tests exercising D9's profile-declared-edge cycle, its cyclic-exempt variant, the gating fix for undeclared built-in edge kinds, the gap in `uses` coverage for a data_flow-sourced edge, and the same dead-zone shape for `depends_on` from a project-scoped requirement. That makes ten DAGChecker fixture shapes, not four, and D9 — one of "the remaining DAG scenarios [with] no dedicated fixture" per the Setup paragraph — now has one, so claim (1) is stale. `dag_project_req_cycle` carries no profile.json, so it runs on the default profile; `CheckDAG` on it returns `project.json:/requirements  depends_on cycle: Project requirement A -> Project requirement B -> Project requirement A`. That message names none of module/requirement/component dependency, falsifying claim (2), and it is a fourth default-profile graph that actually cycles (the built-in `dag_req_cycle` path still reports `requirement dependency cycle` and is unaffected), falsifying claim (3)'s "exactly the three".
proposed_fix: Update the Setup paragraph's fixture enumeration to name all ten DAGChecker fixture shapes (dag_valid, dag_module_cycle, dag_req_cycle, dag_comp_cycle, dag_profile_edge_cycle, dag_profile_edge_cyclic_exempt, dag_profile_builtin_exempt, dag_profile_omits_builtin_edges, dag_profile_data_flow_uses_cycle, dag_project_req_cycle), and remove D9 from "the remaining DAG scenarios have no dedicated fixture" since it is now covered by dag_profile_edge_cycle, dag_profile_edge_cyclic_exempt, dag_profile_omits_builtin_edges, dag_profile_data_flow_uses_cycle and dag_project_req_cycle. Update arch_dag_checker.md's "Graphs Checked" paragraph to name a fourth default-profile-cycling graph (project-scoped requirement dependency) alongside module/requirement/component dependency, and adjust its message-naming sentence to cover the generic path's message shape (`<edge kind> cycle: ...`) rather than only the three built-in graphs' fixed names. Update D9's closing clause from "exactly the three the scenarios above exercise, the other four passing vacuously" to "exactly module, requirement (module- and project-scoped), and component dependency, the other four edge kinds passing vacuously".
